name: Tensor Product Attention (TPA)

source.title: Tensor Product Attention Is All You Need

oneLiner: Factorise Q/K/V into contextual low-rank tensor products so the KV cache shrinks — a cousin of MLA.

name: MiniMax-01 — lightning (linear) attention hybrid at 456B

source.title: MiniMax-01: Scaling Foundation Models with Lightning Attention

problem: 1M-token training and 4M-token inference: softmax is O(L²) with linear KV growth; linear attention was cheap but its causal cumsum was slow in practice.
idea: Lightning attention (an I/O-efficient tiled linear attention) in 7 of every 8 layers, one softmax layer in 8, plus MoE.
buys: First frontier-scale linear-attention ship; trained to 1M, claims 4M NIAH; 7/8 of layers carry constant state
costs: 1/8 layers still full softmax so the KV cache is ~8× smaller, not gone; recall leans on those layers
Custom kernels; MiniMax's own M2 (Oct 2025) went back to full attention citing infra immaturity and eval blind spots

agent1m.why: 256K–4M where decode memory dominates and you can afford a mixed-layer stack

pickWhen.verdict: The proof of concept for hybrids at scale — and the M2 retreat is the honest footnote.

name: RoPE to NoPE and Back Again — RoPE-SWA + NoPE-global hybrid

source.title: Rope to Nope and Back Again: A New Hybrid Attention Strategy
source.authors: Yang, Venkitesh, Talupuru, Lin, Cairuz, Blunsom, Locatelli (Cohere)

firstShipped.model: Cohere Command R7B (3 SWA-RoPE : 1 global NoPE) — shipped six weeks before the paper; then Command A (111B, 256K, Mar 2025)

problem: Pure RoPE degrades beyond training length; pure NoPE trains fine but is weaker at short range. Wanted 128–256K with less KV and better length generalisation.
idea: 1:3 full:SWA — three sliding-window (4,096) RoPE layers, then one full-attention layer with *no* positional encoding; QK-Norm removed.
buys: At 256K, needle 9.97 vs 8.25 and RULER-retrieval −22% vs −41% for the baseline going 8K→256K; KV of 3/4 layers bounded by the window
The NoPE-every-4th-layer half is what SmolLM3 took; Llama 4 iRoPE follows it in spirit; the full SWA-RoPE + NoPE-global recipe shipped in Cohere's Command R7B / Command A
costs: NoPE global layers rely on causal-mask-implied position — fragile at short range; the SWA layers must supply locality
1/4 of layers still O(L) KV; ratio and window are tuned

coding128k.why: training from scratch for 128K+ with a ~4× KV cut

agent1m.why: the position half of the 2025 hybrid recipe

pickWhen.verdict: Positions get out of the way: RoPE where locality matters, none where reach matters.

name: TransMLA — converting GQA checkpoints to MLA

source.title: TransMLA: Multi-Head Latent Attention Is All You Need

oneLiner: Shows GQA is a special case of MLA and converts GQA models to MLA post-hoc — the retrofit path for the smallest KV cache.
whyFootnote: A conversion of an existing node.

name: NSA — Native Sparse Attention (DeepSeek): compress + select + slide

source.title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention

firstShipped.model: Not shipped as-is; DeepSeek's shipped sparse mechanism is DSA (V3.2-Exp), a different design

problem: Most recent sparse methods (H2O, Quest, MInference…) applied sparsity only at inference on a dense-pretrained backbone, and the trainable dynamic ones had non-differentiable or non-contiguous selection; fixed-pattern sparsity (Sparse Transformer, Longformer) trained end-to-end but could not adapt to content. Wanted: learned, dynamic selection that is trainable end-to-end *and* hardware-aligned across training, prefill and decode — FlashAttention's lesson applied to sparsity.
idea: Three branches per query, gated by a small MLP: (1) *compressed* coarse tokens (block 32, stride 16), (2) *selected* fine-grained top-n blocks (block 64, n=16 incl. 1 initial + 2 local), (3) a *sliding window* (512). Group-centric kernels so all heads in a GQA group share the block selection.
buys: vs a Triton FlashAttention-2 on A100 at 64K: 9.0× forward and 6.0× backward measured; the 11.6× decode figure is an expected speedup from KV memory-access volume — and it matches or beats full attention on benchmarks (27B MoE, 3B active)
The first learned, dynamic-selection sparse attention with hardware-aligned kernels for training, prefill and decode (fixed patterns had trained fast since 2019; content-based selection had not)
The compressed / selected / window trinity that reads like a summary of the whole timeline
costs: Three branches = extra parameters, kernels and engineering; block-level selection is coarse
Needs GQA/MQA sharing to be hardware-efficient (all heads in a group must share the selection)
Benefits show mainly at long sequences (speedups quoted at 64K); not what DeepSeek actually shipped

coding128k.why: pretraining a 64K+ model where attention dominates and you own the kernel stack

pickWhen.verdict: Right when you pretrain long and own kernels; wrong for a 2K chatbot. Note the honest wrinkle: DeepSeek shipped DSA, not NSA.

name: MoBA — Mixture of Block Attention (Moonshot)

source.title: MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs
source.evidence: [v1] Tue, 18 Feb 2025 14:06:05 UTC — two days after NSA

firstShipped.model: Kimi long-context serving ('already been deployed to support Kimi's long-context requests')

problem: Sparse long-context prefill/training at 32K–1M with *no* new parameters, so a model can switch between full and sparse.
idea: Mean-pool keys per block; each query top-k gates over blocks by q·mean(K_block); always attend to the own block; FlashAttention-style kernels. 8K/32K: block 512, top-3 (~81–95% sparse); 1M: block 4096, top-12.
buys: No added parameters; smooth transition between full and sparse; deployed in Kimi's long-context serving
costs: Block-mean pooling is a crude relevance proxy (misses single needle tokens); non-differentiable top-k gate
Saves compute, not KV (full cache still stored); real gains only at long sequences

rag32k.why: the paper's 32K config (block 512, top-3) is first-class; the wall-clock gain is modest there and KV is unchanged

coding128k.why: existing full-attention model, cheap long prefill, dense fallback

pickWhen.verdict: NSA's same-week sibling: less machinery, same bet — read only a few blocks of the million.

name: Gemma 3 — 5:1 local:global, 1K window, 128K

source.title: Gemma 3 Technical Report
source.evidence: Google blog 'Introducing Gemma 3' dated March 12, 2025; report [v1] Tue, 25 Mar 2025 15:52:34 UTC — '5 local layers for every global layer', local span 1024, RoPE base 1M on global / 10K on local

problem: Going from 8K to 128K: with Gemma 2's 1:1 ratio and 4K window the KV overhead was ~60% at 32K.
idea: Five local layers (window 1,024) for every global layer; RoPE base 1M on global layers, 10K on local; QK-Norm replaces soft-capping.
buys: KV overhead at 32K from ~60% to <15% with minimal perplexity impact; 128K context in 4B–27B open models with no new kernels
costs: Only 1 layer in 6 sees the whole context; a 1K window hard-codes locality
Global layers still pay full O(L) KV; ratio and window re-tuned per family

pickWhen.verdict: The 2025 default for open weights: most layers cheap, a few global.

name: Llama 4 iRoPE — interleaved NoPE layers + attention temperature

source.title: The Llama 4 herd (Meta blog); no arXiv paper
source.evidence: Meta blog dated April 5, 2025: 'the use of interleaved attention layers without positional embeddings' and 'inference time temperature scaling of attention'; HF config: NoPE every 4th layer, chunked attention 8192 on RoPE layers, QK-norm

firstShipped.model: Llama 4 Scout (10M-token claim, trained at 256K) / Maverick

problem: A marketable 10M context from 256K training, and bounded attention cost in most layers.
idea: RoPE in most layers with chunked (8,192) attention; every 4th layer has no positional embedding and attends globally; inference-time attention temperature scaling for length generalisation.
buys: NoPE-in-production at frontier scale; the same family as Cohere's RNoPE-SWA and SWAN
costs: Meta's prose omits that the NoPE layers are the global ones — that comes from the released config
Practical quality far below 10M was widely questioned; temperature scaling is a heuristic; chunked (not sliding) attention has hard boundaries

agent1m.why: treat 10M as extrapolation, not trained capability

pickWhen.verdict: The biggest lab endorsing 'no positions on the reach layers'.

name: SWAN-GPT — NoPE + sliding-window RoPE, retrofit-able

source.title: SWAN-GPT: An Efficient and Scalable Approach for Long-Context Language Modeling

problem: Extrapolation without long-context training, and conversion of existing pretrained models.
idea: One global NoPE layer then three sliding-window (512) RoPE layers, repeated; inference-time log-scaling of the NoPE layers' scores; existing decoders convert with ~2% of pretraining (315B tokens at 32K for an 8B model).
buys: Strong extrapolation with no long-context training; a conversion path for existing models
costs: Relies on an inference-time score-scaling heuristic; NoPE layers still full-KV; research scale

coding128k.why: you already have a RoPE model and want cheap long-context conversion

pickWhen.verdict: Same design family as Cohere (Jan) and Llama 4 (Apr 5); the retrofit-friendly one.

name: Multi-Token Attention

source.title: Multi-Token Attention

oneLiner: Convolutions over queries, keys and heads so neighbouring tokens jointly decide attention — more quality for more compute.
whyFootnote: Moves the bill the wrong way; quality tweak.

name: Softpick — rectified, non-sum-to-one softmax

source.title: Softpick: No Attention Sink, No Massive Activations with Rectified Softmax

oneLiner: A trained alternative to softmax-1: zero attention sinks, no massive activations.

name: Gated Attention — sink-free softmax attention (Qwen)

source.title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free

firstShipped.model: Qwen3-Next (the 'Gated Attention' layers of the 3:1 hybrid)

problem: Attention sinks and massive activations are a by-product of softmax having to sum to one; heads cannot abstain.
idea: A head-specific sigmoid gate applied after scaled dot-product attention — non-linearity plus sparsity, and no attention sink forms.
buys: Sink-free training, better extrapolation; the softmax layers Qwen3-Next ships
costs: Extra gate parameters and an elementwise op; a training-time choice, not a retrofit

chatbot2k.why: cheap and stable in a new pretraining run

pickWhen.verdict: The 2025 answer to the 2023 sink question: fix the softmax instead of pinning a token.

name: Grouped-Tied / Grouped Latent Attention (decode-efficient MLA)

source.title: Hardware-Efficient Attention for Fast Decoding

oneLiner: Tie K and V or shard the latent so MLA-class caches decode with better tensor-parallel arithmetic intensity.

name: MiniCPM4 / InfLLM v2 — trainable sparse attention on-device

source.title: MiniCPM4: Ultra-Efficient LLMs on End Devices

oneLiner: Trainable block-sparse attention for long context on end devices — NSA's idea at 8B on a phone.

name: gpt-oss — banded (128) : dense alternation + learned attention sinks

source.title: gpt-oss-120b & gpt-oss-20b Model Card
source.evidence: Model card: release date August 5, 2025; arXiv [v1] Fri, 8 Aug 2025 19:24:38 UTC — 'attention blocks alternate between banded window and fully dense patterns, where the bandwidth is 128 tokens … Each attention head has a learned bias in the denominator of the softmax, similar to off-by-one attention and attention sinks'

problem: KV and compute for 128K in an open MoE, plus stability: let heads attend to nothing without wasting a real token.
idea: Alternate banded-window (128 tokens, following GPT-3) and dense layers; GQA 64/8; RoPE with YaRN to 131,072; a learned per-head bias in the softmax denominator — softmax-1 with the 1 made learnable.
buys: Half the layers' KV is tiny; the sink logit is one scalar per head and worth copying into any new model
costs: Half the layers see only 128 tokens, so long-range work falls on the dense half
Sinks needed kernel support (FlashAttention / vLLM added it); YaRN-extended rather than natively trained at 128K

rag32k.why: the simplest KV win on a single GPU class

pickWhen.verdict: Three timeline threads in one model card: Sparse Transformer's banded layers, StreamingLLM's sinks, and Evan Miller's off-by-one.

name: Qwen3-Next — 3:1 Gated DeltaNet : Gated Attention

source.title: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (model card)
source.evidence: HF repo initial commit 9 Sep 2025, public announcement 11 Sep 2025 (vLLM 'Now Supports Qwen3-Next' post dated Sep 11, 2025); model card: '12 * (3 * (Gated DeltaNet -> MoE) -> 1 * (Gated Attention -> MoE))', 262,144 native context

problem: 256K native (1M via YaRN) prefill and decode throughput for a 3B-active MoE; standard attention was the bottleneck at 32K+.
idea: 48 layers: three Gated DeltaNet layers, then one Gated Attention layer (16 Q / 2 KV heads, head dim 256, RoPE on 64 dims), each followed by MoE; multi-token prediction.
buys: First frontier-family ship of the delta rule; Qwen claims ~10× throughput vs Qwen3-32B at 32K+
costs: 1/4 layers still full-attention KV; linear-state recall limits; needs FLA / hybrid KV-manager kernels; launch-time inference-stack bugs
Quality gains vs dense Qwen3-32B are Qwen's own evals

agent1m.why: long-context agent / RAG serving where decode throughput per GPU matters

pickWhen.verdict: The 1960 delta rule ships in a frontier family — 4.5 years after Schlag et al.

name: DSA — DeepSeek Sparse Attention (V3.2): lightning indexer + top-k tokens on MLA

source.title: Introducing DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp (news); DeepSeek-V3.2 tech report
source.evidence: DeepSeek news post dated September 29, 2025 (tech report PDF in github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp); non-Exp V3.2 released 2025-12-01; paper arXiv 2512.02556 [v1] Tue, 2 Dec 2025 09:25:14 UTC

problem: Cut the 128K training and inference cost of a 671B MLA model *without pretraining from scratch* — and cut the API price.
idea: A *lightning indexer* (few heads, ReLU, FP8) scores every key for the current query cheaply; select the top-k = 2,048 latent KV entries; run MLA in MQA mode over just those. Continued-pretrained from V3.1-Terminus: 1,000 dense warm-up steps training only the indexer, then 15,000 sparse steps (~944B tokens). O(L·k) attention.
buys: Near-identical quality to Terminus at 128K with attention O(L·k); the API price halved the day it shipped
Token-level (not block-level) selection — the 2019 top-k idea finally with a cheap way to *find* the top k
Retrofit-able onto an existing large model — demonstrated (V3.1-Terminus → V3.2-Exp), the property GQA had; NSA never tested one
costs: The indexer still scans all L keys per query (cheap, but O(L²) in a small dimension); fixed k regardless of need; benefit only beyond a few thousand tokens
Requires MLA/MQA-style shared KV to make selection efficient; new kernels (TileLang / DeepGEMM / FlashMLA-sparse)
Shipped as 'experimental' first; DSA is *not* NSA — no compressed or sliding-window branches

coding128k.why: existing large MLA model, 128K serving cost

agent1m.why: V3.2 is trained and served at 128K; the indexer is still O(L²) per query and k=2,048 is 0.2% of 1M — nothing in the report tests beyond 128K (V4's compression is the 1M answer)

pickWhen.verdict: Right for a big MLA model you already have and serve long; wrong for anything short. The most literal 'pay less of the bill' entry on the timeline.

name: Kimi Linear / KDA — channel-wise gated delta rule + NoPE MLA, 3:1

source.title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture
source.evidence: [v1] 30 Oct 2025; HF moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct initial commit October 30, 2025

problem: KV memory and decode throughput at 1M for agentic / RL workloads; Gated DeltaNet's per-head scalar gate was too coarse.
idea: KDA: each feature dimension keeps its own forgetting rate over the delta rule (diagonal-plus-low-rank transitions, chunkwise kernel); 3 KDA layers per full MLA layer; NoPE on the MLA layers so the recurrent layers carry position.
buys: Up to 75% less KV; 2.3× lower time-per-token at 1M (batch 1) and up to ~6× decode throughput once the freed memory is spent on larger batches
costs: Still 1/4 layers full MLA, so KV and decode time keep growing there (the hybrid's I/O-bound gain is capped by the layer ratio); DPLR chunk kernel more complex than GDN; 3B-active scale, not frontier

agent1m.why: finer-grained forgetting for long agent traces

pickWhen.verdict: Qwen3-Next's recipe plus Cohere's NoPE-on-global — the two 2025 threads braided in one model.

name: Compressed Convolutional Attention (CCA) — attention inside a compressed latent

source.title: Compressed Convolutional Attention: Efficient Attention in a Compressed Latent Space
source.evidence: arXiv API published 2025-10-06T04:24:23Z (v1); shipped in ZAYA1-base (HF initial commit 19 Nov 2025) and ZAYA1-8B (May 2026, '8× KV-cache compression')

oneLiner: Runs the whole attention computation in a shared compressed latent space (parameters, prefill compute and KV all shrink); shipped in Zyphra's ZAYA1 models.

name: Grouped Differential Attention (Motif-2-12.7B)

source.title: Motif 2 12.7B technical report

oneLiner: Differential Transformer's first shipped descendant: asymmetric head groups for signal-preserving vs noise-suppressing attention, in a 12.7B open model.
whyFootnote: Quality tweak; adoption of a node.

name: Nested Learning / HOPE — attention and Titans as memory modules at different update rates

source.title: Introducing Nested Learning (Google Research blog); paper 'Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architectures'
source.evidence: Google Research blog dated Nov 7, 2025; arXiv API published 2025-12-31T07:59:43Z (v1)

oneLiner: Frames attention, Titans and optimisers as associative-memory modules updated at different frequencies; HOPE = a self-modifying Titans plus a continuum of memory modules for continual learning.
whyFootnote: Research framework; the Titans line already has a node.

name: OLMo 3 — 3:1 sliding-window : global, YaRN on global layers only (fully open)

source.title: Olmo 3 (Ai2 blog)
source.evidence: Ai2 blog dated November 20, 2025; Olmo3Config sliding_window 4096, 3 of every 4 layers windowed, final layer full

oneLiner: A fully open model adopting the local:global recipe (window 4096, 3:1) with QK-Norm and YaRN applied only to the global layers.
